flawed_step: Lemma metabelian_injectivity (lines 0530-0536: 'for all non-zero v in V_0, ad(v): gr_i(Lbar) -> gr_{i+1}(Lbar) is injective'), and the step of the proof of Lemma silly_injectivity that invokes it (line 0560: 'By Lemma metabelian_injectivity, ad(v) is injective when restricted to \oplus_{\alpha\in A} L_{\alpha,n}'), which makes the stated conclusion of Lemma silly_injectivity ('for all i<n, there is an injection W_i^{c=-1} -> W_{i+1}/W_{i+1}^{c=-1}', lines 0539-0551) false at i=1.
counterexample:
Degree-1 failure of ad(v). Take V_0 = Q_p x_1 + Q_p x_2 (dim 2 > 1) and Lbar the free metabelian Lie algebra on V_0. Then gr_1(Lbar) = V_0 (dim 2) and gr_2(Lbar) = wedge^2 V_0 (dim 1). For v = x_1 != 0, ad(x_1)(x_1) = [x_1,x_1] = 0, so ad(x_1): gr_1 -> gr_2 has a 1-dimensional kernel; indeed no injective map gr_1 -> gr_2 exists at all since 2 > 1. So Lemma metabelian_injectivity is false as stated (it asserts injectivity for every i, with no restriction to i >= 2).

This propagates to a counterexample to Lemma silly_injectivity itself, in the very family the paper's case (1) is about. Take K = Q (one embedding alpha = id, so the Weil-restriction decomposition is trivial), X = P^1 - {0,1,infinity}, n = 2. Then V = L_1 = H^1_et(X_{Qbar},Q_p)^* = Q_p(1)^2, on which complex conjugation c acts by -1 (c acts by -1 on Q_p(1)); hence V^{c=1} = 0 and V^{c=-1} = V. Take W = L_1 = V, which satisfies the hypothesis (its projection to L_1(X_{Kbar,alpha}) is surjective). Then:
  W_1 = W = V, so W_1^{c=-1} = V has dimension 2;
  W_2 = image of W^{tensor 2} under the commutator = gr_2 = wedge^2 V = Q_p(2), of dimension 1, on which c acts by (-1)^2 = +1, so W_2^{c=-1} = 0 and W_2/W_2^{c=-1} has dimension 1.
The lemma claims an injection W_1^{c=-1} -> W_2/W_2^{c=-1}, i.e. an injection of a 2-dimensional space into a 1-dimensional space: impossible.

The proof's mechanism visibly breaks here as well: the set A of infinite places where W_1^{c=-1} projects nontrivially is the single real place of Q; every nonzero v in W satisfies the requirement pi_alpha(v) not in V^{c=1} = 0, yet for every such v one has ad(v)(v) = [v,v] = 0 with v in W_1^{c=-1} nonzero, so ad(v) is never injective on W_1^{c=-1}.
reasoning_summary: I looked for the riskiest concrete (finite-dimensional, checkable) claims. The metabelian-Lie-algebra lemmas in Section 6 are the only fully explicit linear-algebra statements. Lemma metabelian_injectivity asserts ad(v) is injective on every graded piece gr_i of a free metabelian Lie algebra (dim V_0 > 1) for every nonzero v in V_0; this is false in degree i = 1 because ad(v)(v) = [v,v] = 0, and for dim V_0 = 2 it fails even for dimension reasons (dim gr_1 = 2 > 1 = dim gr_2 = dim wedge^2 V_0). Lemma silly_injectivity invokes exactly this ('ad(v) is injective when restricted to \oplus_{alpha in A} L_{alpha,n}') and asserts an injection W_i^{c=-1} -> W_{i+1}/W_{i+1}^{c=-1} for all i < n; the instance K = Q, X = P^1 - {0,1,infinity}, W = L_1 = Q_p(1)^2, i = 1 refutes the stated conclusion outright (2-dimensional source, 1-dimensional target). I verified the c-actions (c = -1 on Q_p(1), hence +1 on gr_2 = wedge^2 V = Q_p(2)) and the graded dimensions of the free metabelian Lie algebra on two generators (dim gr_1 = 2, dim gr_i = i - 1 for i >= 2, from the Koszul syzygy module description the paper itself gives in Lemma metabelian_module). Scope note, stated for honesty: the downstream uses of Lemma silly_injectivity (case (1), line 0627, and case (2) under Bloch-Kato, line 0689) only need the conclusion 'for infinitely many i', and the failure I exhibit is confined to i = 1 (for i >= 2 the graded dimensions are nondecreasing), so the finiteness theorems are likely recoverable by restricting both lemmas to i >= 2. Nevertheless, as written the document asserts and uses two lemmas that admit the explicit counterexample above, so the proof text is not correct as stated. Per the counterexample-first protocol I stopped auditing at this point and did not verify the remainder (Sections on Jannsen/Bloch-Kato deductions, case (3), case (4)); note also that the supplied excerpt omits source lines 123-1221, so several referenced definitions were unavailable.
